### The End of Exile
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/end-exile
Passage: Matthew 2:16-18
Points:
- King Herod ordered the slaughter of young boys in Bethlehem out of paranoid desire to preserve his throne.
- The mothers' sorrow fulfilled Jeremiah 31:15, recalling the ancient grief of Rachel over Israel's exile.
- This tragedy demonstrated that God's people remained in exilic suffering despite living in the Promised Land.
- Jesus' arrival marks the end of exile and inaugurates the promised new covenant.
- Persecutors may inflict severe harm, but they can never overturn God's sovereign redemptive plans.

### It Is Written
Author: Wendy Stringer
Site: The Gospel Coalition Canada
URL: https://ca.thegospelcoalition.org/article/it-is-written-2/
Passage: Matthew 2:18
Points:
- Jeremiah 31:15 foretold the unbearable lamentation and weeping that would occur in Bethlehem.
- The slaughter of the innocent boys did not happen beyond God's notice or outside His sovereign knowledge.
- Jesus entered a dark and violent world, sharing our exposure to grief and deep loss.
- God attentively records every tear and never overlooks the agony of grieving parents.
- Prophetic fulfillment assures believers that God is actively working to bring ultimate healing to a weeping world.
